All these three teams are showing themselves capable of inclusion in our scratch teams; and as stated previously, it is through the medium of our club handicaps that we are able to find out what talent we have available. The 220 yards resulted in a win for F.
Given time, we are sure this pleasantly situated ground will prove popular with the South London athletes. In the first event, the 4 x 100 yards, we fielded quite a useful team; and, with F.
Roberts, the young Mitcham runner, trailed his man well, but nearing home Herbert went away to win in convincing fashion. Our team in the 4 x 300 yards started off well, F.
The Club 3 Miles Championship was also decided, and in addition we had two races open to unattached novices on the programme. Tom Wiley won the 100 yards match, with F.

On the programme was the first of the series of four contests for the Inter-Club Relay Shield, of which we are the holders, and also three club handicaps. In the 4 x 100 yards we started, as we hope to finish, by winning this event, our runners being Tom Wiley, Les Bennett, F.
In the 100 yards there were many absentees and with one heat a walk-over, and some of the others with two or three runners only, we had a final of 5 runners—all “Bels.” F.
It is with deep regret that we have to announce the death of Frank William (Billy) Pritchard. Billy was a Lieutenant in the Anti-Tank Regt. and was killed action in North Africa on November 26th.
Belgrave entries for that meeting included E Gray (100 yds) T D Wiley (100 yds) reserves F W Pritchard and S C Botwright. 440 yds D G Michael, H E Pack, reserves T H Scrimshaw & A A Bird.
